$comment: Single source of truth for the FFmpeg engine the app links against (issue #270).
build-ffmpeg-engine.ts, verify-ffmpeg-engine.ts and plugins/ffmpeg-kit-plugin.js all
read this file. Do not restate a version, a flag or a URL anywhere else.
artifacts.*.sha256 identifies the bytes we published. It is not a bit-reproducibility
check: FFmpeg embeds its configure line, and that line carries the build directory and
a build-date stamp. Verification refuses anything that is not the published artifact.
Where we publish the build, and therefore where the LGPL corresponding-source
offer points. The consuming app repository is private, so an EAS build could not
fetch a release asset from it without a credential on the build path. This
repository is public, names no product, and carries only the LGPL work plus the
recipe.
Tags read v<upstream version>-<rebuild number> and are never moved: each names an
exact set of bytes, so any rebuild takes the next number.
The in-app attributions screen repeats this URL; src/lib/ffmpeg-attribution.test.ts
fails if the two ever disagree.
No --enable-gpl anywhere. The GPL-only extras of the retired full-gpl build
(libx264, libx265, libxvid, vid.stab, rubberband) are unreferenced in this
codebase, so the flag buys nothing and costs the whole GPL exposure.
--enable-libass transitively enables freetype, fribidi, fontconfig, harfbuzz,
expat, libuuid and libiconv (scripts/function.sh, enable_library libass).
freetype and fontconfig are still listed explicitly so a future libass change
cannot silently drop the drawtext= dependency.

$archComment: x86-64 is the Intel simulator slice. It is built even though no shipped app
uses it: without it, Xcode on an Intel Mac fails to find the framework headers
and reports a missing include, which reads like a broken install rather than a
missing slice. arm64e and Mac Catalyst stay off — the app ships to neither.

$comment: Why each enabled component exists. Every entry was swept out of src/ and app/;
nothing here is aspirational. Remove a component only after an on-device pass
over the stage that names it.
Decoders, demuxers and muxers the app needs (h264, hevc, mpeg4, aac, alac, mp3,
png, mjpeg, mov/mp4, wav, image2) are built into FFmpeg and need no flag.
usage.libass: subtitles= caption burn-in, including the ASS positioning tags the editorial presets emit
usage.fontconfig: font fallback for libass; drawtext itself uses fontfile=
usage.ios-videotoolbox: hevc_videotoolbox, the Stage 1 encoder on iOS
usage.zlib: PNG overlay stills and mov/mp4 handling
usage.libiconv: text encoding for libass and fontconfig
usage.android-media-codec: Android hardware decode; the Android encoder path is tracked separately in issue #43
